title: Book: The Intelligent Investor — Benjamin Graham (1949)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Benjamin Graham's classic separates investing from speculation: an investment promises safety of principal and an adequate return after thorough analysis, while everything else is speculation. Two ideas are famous. 'Mr. Market' is an imaginary business partner who offers to buy or sell you his share every day at moods-driven prices; you can ignore him or exploit his extremes, but you should never let him dictate your view of value. 'Margin of safety' means buying only when the price is well below your conservative estimate of worth, so mistakes and bad luck do not sink you. Graham also distinguishes the defensive investor (diversified, simple, low-effort) from the enterprising investor (does deep research). Warren Buffett has publicly praised it. Cautions: it is dense, written for US markets of an earlier era, and the stock-screening numbers are dated; the lasting value is the mindset, not the formulas.
